title: Deploy a static site to any static host
when: The user has a built HTML, CSS and JS site and wants to publish it to a static host or a plain web server with correct caching and no broken links.
prompt:
Goal: A repeatable deploy of dist/ with hashed asset names, correct cache headers, a real 404 page and a check after upload.
Steps:
1. Build into an empty dist/; stop if the build fails or dist/index.html is missing.
2. Fingerprint assets (app.3f9c1a.css) so they can be cached for a year; HTML keeps stable names.
3. Headers: Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable on hashed assets; no-cache on HTML and the service worker; correct types for .webmanifest, .svg and .wasm.
4. Ship 404.html served with status 404; a single page app falls back to index.html for routes only, never for missing assets.
5. Upload with the host's CLI or rsync -avz --delete dist/ user@host:/var/www/site/, first with --dry-run, reading the deletions.
6. Upload assets first and HTML last, so no live page points at a missing file.
7. Afterwards request three key URLs, expect 200 and the new version string, and run a link check.
8. Archive the previous dist/ for rollback.
Quality bar:
- No visitor sees an unstyled page mid deploy.
- A deploy with no changes uploads almost nothing.
- Every internal link resolves.
Pitfalls:
- --delete aimed at the wrong remote folder.
- Long caching on HTML, so visitors keep old pages for days.
- Root relative links that break under a subpath.
Verify:
- [ ] Dry run step present.
- [ ] Cache rules differ for hashed assets and HTML.
- [ ] 404 page exists.
- [ ] Post deploy check runs.
Output: scripts/deploy.sh, the host header config file and a Deploy section in README.md.

examples.input: publicar meu site estatico com cache certo
examples.output: deploy.sh: clean build, rsync --dry-run then real, assets before HTML, immutable cache for hashed files, no-cache for HTML, link check
